title: Market intel hypothesis hub and model-coverage prioritizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a lightweight 'Hypothesis Hub' and a model-coverage prioritizer that lets PMs and platform teams rapidly identify gaps in model coverage for high-value enterprise signals (latency-sensitive embeddings, instruction tuning, on-prem compatibility).

Scope:
- Ingest upstream signals (public model releases, vendor roadmaps, benchmark publications, partner telemetry, and customer requests).
- Create a small, extensible schema for hypotheses (trigger, affected product surface, severity, confidence, proposed mitigation).
- Implement a scoring heuristic that ranks models by coverage gap likelihood and enterprise impact (configurable weights for latency, cost, security posture, and feature parity).
- Deliverables: a Confluence PRD with scoring rubric, a CSV ingest prototype and dashboard slice in existing market-intel dashboard, and a 6-week cadence plan for signal refresh and stakeholder reviews.

Why this matters: Current scouting is ad-hoc and heavily memory-driven across PMs and solutions teams. This work standardizes signal capture and gives a reproducible prioritizer so engineering and procurement can pre-commit to capacity / vendor playbooks ahead of vendor outages or rapid model deprecation.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence PRD with explicit fields and scoring rubric reviewed by eng and solutions (approved)
Prototype ingest of 3 signal sources (model release RSS, internal telemetry alert feed, competitor pricing CSV) into a canonical CSV with timestamp and confidence columns
Priority list generated for top 25 enterprise use-cases with justification and scoring breakdown
Dashboard tile added to market-intel dashboard showing top 10 emergent gaps (refreshable weekly)
Runbook for triage: when a gap score > 0.75, trigger playbooks for provisioning Dedicated capacity or initiating fallback rollout
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: aligned on goals with GTM, Solutions, and Eng infra. Proposal: start with 3 signal sources to prove concept.
2026-03-03 - Eng feedback (K. Morales): prefer a schema that captures quantization/precision compatibility flags to map to runtime constraints.
2026-03-05 - Data team (J. Nguyen) shared a sandbox feed of customer latency complaints (anonymized) and suggested adding 'observed_customer_count' to the ingest schema.
2026-03-07 - PM review (S. Roberts): clarified that 'cost' should be normalized to $/1k tokens for parity across providers; agreed to use median 30-day pricing.
2026-03-09 - Design input (M. Alvarez): recommended a compact 'gap card' UI that shows cause, score drivers, and quick actions (notify procurement / schedule bench run).
2026-03-10 - Prototype: CSV ingest and scoring script pushed to GH branch (see links). Smoke test shows top gaps align with field reports.
2026-03-12 - Decision log: initial scoring weights set to Latency:40, Cost:25, Security/On-prem:20, Feature Parity:15. Rationale: latency-sensitive customers are top ARR risk.
Next: schedule 30-min review with SRE and Solutions on 2026-03-18 to validate remediation playbooks and capacity triggers.
decisions: Start scope limited to enterprise-facing signals (exclude consumer-only models for v1)
Scoring weights finalized for v1: Latency 40 / Cost 25 / Security/On-prem 20 / Feature parity 15
Weekly refresh cadence for signal ingestion and monthly review cycle for thresholds
Runbook trigger threshold set at 0.75 for high-priority follow-up actions
notes_on_tradeoffs:
Depth vs breadth: v1 focuses on enterprise signals (depth) to produce actionable playbooks; subsequent waves will expand coverage to SMB and open-source community signals.
Scoring transparency: expose driver contributions to avoid black-box decisions; heavier engineering investment needed if automated remediation is desired (vs. manual ops alerts).
Data freshness vs accuracy: weekly refresh chosen to balance noise and operational churn; high-confidence signals will be flagged for immediate review regardless of cadence.
